steps.what: List security needs at each location
Assess security needs before deployment
Draft where staff and technology should sit

loop.input: assessment notes and the plan template
loop.output: a plan that names location and resource type
loop.check: Every location id is on the extract
loop.stop: Stop a row that names a person to watch
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a location needs the resource is not a formula

steps.what: Sign the deployment of those resources
File the signed deployment plan

tasks.design: The loss prevention manager assesses security needs at each location before any deployment of staff or technology. A draft in {DOCS} may list locations and the resources already there. The manager signs where staff and technology should go. The plan names locations and resource types. It does not watch named staff. A design that does needs a separate consent decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Deployment was agreed in a call, so a store could not show why a person or a device was placed there.
tasks.enabler_now: A location row can hold current staff hours and the devices already installed.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a location needs more people or more technology is a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager assesses the needs and signs the only deployment that may proceed.

ambition.what: Sign a deployment when a location's needs are listed, not once a year

tasks.altitude: Less time assembling the location list. The assessment stays with the manager.

reach.task: Host only the resources named in the signed deployment
reach.learn: Which version applies to that location

evidence.claim: Deploying loss prevention resources is a location list and a judgement about people and technology. The list is not the decision.
Digest [S2] describes a governance register. Here it holds location and resource rows, not a watch of the shop floor.

Digest [S12] says works council consent is required before monitoring staff. This plan names locations and resource types. A design that watches named staff is a separate consent decision and is not this task.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. Placing a person on a rota is a later scheduling task.
Input contract: location id, current staff hours, current devices, requested change. Producer is the location list. A location with no current figures is assessed by hand.
Use the document store before a custom planner. Do not score staff.
unknowns: Which locations will open or close this year.
research_questions: How often does the signed deployment differ from the first draft?

already_counted.description: The assessment stays with the manager

incremental.description: Update a location row when a device is removed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes location figures are missing, so the assessment is done from memory. The high case saves the list assembly only. The judgement and the sign-off are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Open physical security standards and procedures
Monitor compliance with inventory control procedures
Show how the procedure is done
Note gaps against physical security standards
Sign the compliance note for those standards

tasks.design: The loss prevention manager monitors compliance with operational, safety and inventory control procedures, including physical security standards. The standards sit in {DOCS}. The check is a visit or a walk-through. Gaps are noted against the standard. A gap that names a person is signed by the manager and is not an automatic finding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Compliance was a memory of the last visit, so a failed procedure had no standard id.
tasks.enabler_now: A standard can be cited by id while the gap is written.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing whether a procedure is really followed takes a person on site.
tasks.human_edge: The manager monitors the compliance and signs the note.
tasks.altitude: The visit stays the work. The note is tied to a standard instead of a loose remark.

reach.task: Show the procedure the manager asks about

evidence.claim: Procedure compliance in stores is a visit against a written standard. A dashboard does not see the shop floor.
Digest [S1] describes a versioned policy library. The standard cited on the note comes from that kind of row. The visit still decides the gap.
Digest [S9] says a decision about a person must not rest on automation alone. A failed procedure is signed by the manager if it names someone.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The store supervisor shows the procedure.
Input contract: store id, standard id, procedure name. Producer is the standards set. A standard with no id is checked by hand.
This is a visit, not a hidden watch of named staff.
unknowns: Which standards the stores have been trained on.
research_questions: What share of gaps are a missing standard rather than a missed procedure?

already_counted.description: The on-site check stays with the manager

incremental.description: Retire a standard that no longer applies

approvals.approved_version: compliance note signed for these standard ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes standards are not filed, so the visit note stays free text. The high case cites a standard id. The visit and the sign-off are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Open the asset list for security systems
Verify maintenance of the burglar alarms
Check closed circuit television and merchandise tags
Sign which systems failed the check
File the signed maintenance result

tasks.design: The loss prevention manager verifies the maintenance of physical security systems: burglar alarms, merchandise tags, and closed circuit television. The check is whether the asset works. It is not a review of who was filmed. Findings are signed against the asset id in {DOCS}. A design that watches named staff is a separate consent decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Maintenance was a vendor sticker, so a dead alarm could sit until the next incident.
tasks.enabler_now: An asset row can hold a last-check date and a pass or fail.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing that an alarm sounds, a tag detaches, or a camera shows the aisle takes a person there.
tasks.human_edge: The manager verifies the assets and signs which systems failed.
tasks.altitude: The check stays on site. The result is an asset row instead of a sticker.

reach.task: Keep the failed asset out of use until it is repaired

evidence.claim: Verifying an alarm, a tag or a camera is a physical check. A register of assets does not replace standing in front of the device.

Digest [S12] says works council consent is required before monitoring staff. This check records whether the asset works. It does not review footage of named people. A design that does is a separate consent decision.
Digest [S15] says generated text has cited facts that were not real. The result note is checked against the assets the manager actually tested.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. Repair by a supplier is a later task.
Input contract: store id, asset id, asset type, last result. Producer is the asset list. An asset with no id is checked and then given an id.
Use the document store's asset list before a custom register.
unknowns: Which assets are on a supplier maintenance contract.
research_questions: What share of failed alarms were already known to the store?

already_counted.description: Checking the alarms stays on site
Checking tags and television stays on site

incremental.description: Add an asset when a store installs a new alarm

approvals.approved_version: maintenance result signed for these asset ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the asset list is incomplete, so the walk still covers everything by eye. The high case opens the list first. The physical check and the sign-off are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the company policies for this visit
Visit stores to check compliance with policies
Walk the procedures with the manager
Sign the visit note on those policies
File the signed store visit note

tasks.design: The loss prevention manager visits stores to check compliance with company policies and procedures. The policies are read from {DOCS} before the visit. The visit stays in the store. The manager signs a note of what was seen. The note is not a remote watch, and it does not replace the visit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visit notes were written days later, so the policy cited and the aisle that was walked could not be tied together.
tasks.enabler_now: A visit can carry a store id, a date and the policy ids that were checked.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing whether a store follows a policy takes the manager in the store.
tasks.human_edge: The manager makes the visit and signs what was found.
tasks.altitude: The visit stays the work. The note names the policies that were checked.

reach.task: Walk the procedures the manager names
reach.learn: Which policy ids were on the visit

evidence.claim: A store visit is time in the store. Preparing the policy list does not perform the visit.
Digest [S1] describes a versioned policy library. The visit note cites those versions. The manager still walks the store.
Digest [S15] says generated text has cited facts that were not real. The visit note is checked against what the manager saw before it is signed.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. Travel sits inside the visit. It is not removed.
Input contract: store id, visit date, policy ids. Producer is the visit plan. A store with no policy list is still visited.
The visit is overt. It is not a hidden watch of named staff.
unknowns: How many stores the manager can physically visit in a week.
research_questions: What share of visit notes are signed on the day of the visit?

already_counted.description: The store visit stays with the manager

incremental.description: Drop a policy from the visit list when it is withdrawn

approvals.approved_version: visit note signed for this store and these policy ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes policies are not filed, so preparation saves nothing and the visit is unchanged. The high case prepares a policy list. The visit and the sign-off are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The manager stops retyping deployment notes and visit sheets, and spends the week in the stores, on the alarms, and on whether the standards are actually being followed.
reach: Store supervisors receive a signed deployment and a visit note instead of a verbal list.
A later audit can see which alarm, tag or camera was checked.
skills_to_grow: Separate a resource plan from the visit that checks it.
Verify an alarm or a tag as an asset, not as a watch of named staff.
Keep the store visit in the store.
role.ambitious_version: Each cycle has a signed deployment, a signed compliance note, a signed asset check and a store visit note from the week it happened.
